note.phase: The full version of this screen is built in phase {{phase}}. Until then it shows the company’s records and every button responds.
note.seeded: {{company}} has {{count}} demo records here, generated from src/data.
note.settingsPhase: Settings editors arrive in phase {{phase}}; each page shows the company’s current values.
note.dashboardPhase: The full widget dashboard (charts, map, alerts, customisation) arrives in phase 4.
note.mobileSignIn: Sign in with a field user's phone, e.g. Yaw: 024 555 1234. The one-time code appears here and in a toast. Or use “Sign in as a persona” in this panel to skip it.
note.settingsLive: Every settings page saves for real: changes show up at once in other tabs, the sidebar, the dashboard and the mobile app. Try Journey 10: remove an approval step, change a loss tolerance, edit a numbering pattern, switch off Inventory.
note.ai: Answers come from scripted intents over this company's own data, with the same permission and module checks as the screens. Try: “Which agents hold the most cash?”, “Farmers with overdue loans”, “Requests priced above list”, “Payouts failed this week”, “Women share of suppliers”. Set VITE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to send unmatched questions to Claude.
note.dashboardLive: Approve, hold or reject straight from “My approvals” — the record, its activity history and the next approver's notifications update everywhere. Customise drags, resizes and adds widgets; save for yourself or as the company default.
note.communities: Communities, their profile answers, leaders, documents and score breakdown come from src/data. Create or edit one: the code comes from the company’s numbering pattern and the data-quality rules run on save. The map pins are coloured by score band.
note.farmers: Saved views cover Women farmers, No consent and Blocked by debt. Register a farmer with a phone that already exists to see the duplicate check. Editing a profile creates a new version, recorded in the history.
note.groups: Upload a meeting record or contribution record in Documents: that manual score is reset and the group goes back to Pending review. Enter the review on the Score tab to complete it. VSLAs have a Savings tab.
note.dataQuality: Select flagged records and Assign to agent: each record becomes a fix task on that agent’s phone (open the mobile window as the agent → Tasks). Fixing it there re-checks the record and resolves the flag here.
note.imports: Journey 15: choose Farmers → Use the sample file. It has 50 rows with 4 errors to fix in the preview, one misspelt community to match, and 3 rows that import but raise data-quality flags.
note.forms: Journey 9: sign in as Aïcha (Kakao Ivoire) → Forms → Profil producteur → add Select one “Certification” using the shared list “Certifications” → Publish. It then appears in web registration, the mobile Register farmer flow, the farmer list’s Columns menu and the Reports field list.
note.builder: Drag types from the palette or click to add. The draft saves as you go; Publish creates the next version, and records keep the version they were captured with. Preview mobile opens the draft in the mobile window.
note.purchaseRequests: Journey 2 (web side): use Page actions in this panel for Yaw’s phone. 1) “Yaw submits a request”. 2) Sign in as Kwame → Approve. 3) Sign in as Efua → Approve, Confirm rate, Pay by mobile money — switch on “Next payout fails” first, then use Retry. 4) “Agent confirms funds received”. 5) “Sync 3 offline purchases” (one voice purchase, a consolidated bag). The request is auto-matched with a small refund: open the Reconciliation tab → Record refund.
note.purchases: Purchases come from agents’ phones (Sync) or the web (Record purchase on a request). Journey 3: Direct-payment purchases → select the 4 unpaid purchases of Yaw’s ticket → Pay 4 by mobile money. Up to the company’s bulk batch size, all from the same request.
note.bags: Every bag code from purchases. Replace a damaged bag: the new code takes the contents, the weight variance and who did it are logged, and the purchases point to the new code.
note.expenses: PRE approvals use the company workflow (Vitara: level 1 automatic, then levels 2–4). Edit is only possible before the first human approval. Paying a PRE whose expense type triggers inbound creates an expected delivery at the agent’s warehouse.
note.reconciliation: Gaps within the company tolerance (Settings → Buying rules) reconcile automatically. Larger gaps are matched and wait for a refund, a top-up or a write-off within the limit.
note.priceBoard: Read-only for managers. Paid prices come from purchases in each zone over the last 30 days. Suggest price uses the median paid price within the tolerance band; apply it in Settings → Price lists.
note.payments: Payments over the company’s checker threshold (Settings → Payments) wait for a second person with the “check” permission — the person who started a payment can’t check it. Two seeded cash advances are waiting: sign in as Ama to approve them. Failed payments have Retry, Unknown ones Check status, successful ones can be marked reversed.
note.wallets: Balances go down with every successful payout and up with reversals, collections and top-ups. Request top-up simulates the treasury transfer: the money lands a few seconds later.
note.mobileSync: Turn “Work offline” on, save a few records, then Sync. “Office edits the record” changes it on the web first, so syncing your edit shows a conflict.

explain.agentCash: For each request where the agent confirmed funds received and that isn't reconciled: money disbursed minus the value of purchases recorded against it. Requests with nothing left are skipped.
explain.topCommunities: Purchased kilograms per community {{period}}, from farmer purchases synced from the mobile app.
explain.overdueLoans: Active loans whose recovery window has ended, with the balance from the loan ledger (company loan terms: interest, penalty and repayment order). Sales from these farmers follow your debt policy: {{policy}}.
explain.aboveList: Open requests whose unit price is above the list price for the agent's zone. Sorted by how far above.
explain.lateReconciliations: Requests where funds were received, the planned purchase date is more than 7 days ago and reconciliation isn't finished.
explain.openDiscrepancies: Inbound deliveries whose received bags or weight differ from what was expected beyond the loss tolerance, and that are not resolved.
explain.agentsBelowTarget: Active agents whose achievement against this week's plan is below 40%.
explain.failedPayouts: Payments with status Failed or Unknown created in the last 7 days (or the most recent ones if none this week).
explain.recoveryByDistrict: Repayments received divided by the principal lent, grouped by the district of each farmer.
explain.plotsMissing: Purchases of commodities marked EUDR-relevant that are not linked to a mapped plot, grouped by community.
explain.noConsent: Farmers whose profile has no consent recording, signature or tick-box.
explain.stockAvailable: Bags with status In stock, summed by warehouse and commodity.
explain.ordersInTransit: Orders and deliveries whose shipment status is In transit.
explain.nurserySurvival: Seedlings alive at the last monitoring round divided by seedlings planted, per batch.
explain.commissionsPending: Commission periods waiting for their first or second approval.
explain.budgetsWaiting: Weekly budget requests waiting for manager or finance review.
explain.carbonSurvival: Trees alive at the last visit divided by trees planted, per carbon project.
explain.topSuppliers: Kilograms on aggregator purchase orders that weren't rejected, per supplier.
explain.womenShare: Share of women among the farmers who sold at least once, and their share of the value paid.
explain.dqByAgent: Farmers flagged by the data-quality rules, grouped by the agent who registered them.
explain.myApprovals: Every purchase request, PRE and aggregator purchase whose current step you can approve, using the company's approval workflows and separation rules.
explain.spendByCommodity: Value and kilograms of farmer purchases {{period}}, per commodity. Average price is value divided by kilograms.
explain.walletBalances: Current balance of each disbursement wallet, compared with its low-balance alert threshold.
explain.riskyRequests: Open requests with at least one risk flag: price above list, agent cash above limit, agent flagged or many requests the same day.
